content.fallback: A1 is a rules-based design system and product workspace. Explore the component registry, build projects with patterns and datasets, review accessibility reports, and use AI helpers inside clear system guardrails.
A1 brings the component registry, editor workflows, labels, accessibility reporting, and AI guardrails into one governed workspace.
Every visible component is defined from the registry, with live configurators, rules, and accessibility reports.
Build projects from A1 components, patterns, datasets, image libraries, and label-driven content.
Structured rules help propose components and generate data-aware pages without inventing patterns.
Reports cover contrast, keyboard behavior, screen reader expectations, and WCAG mappings.
A1 combines project editing, shared assets, data, themes, labels, and rules so teams can build with structure instead of starting from a blank page.
Create and edit governed projects through a JSON page model.
Commonly defined patterns that can be shared within or across projects.
Plug-and-play datasets for binding pages to real content.
Define UI, component, accessibility, and workflow rules for humans and agents.
Lightweight digital asset management for project images and reusable media.
Quick custom icons with upload, validation, and font generation.
Custom themes with a few clicks, from color ramps to typography and semantic roles.
Shared labels and translations for reusable, locale-ready interface text.
120+ components · 10 categories. From typography primitives to complex data tables — everything is tokenized, accessible, responsive, and connected to the live component docs.
The same token foundations power React, pure HTML/CSS, React Native, and Web Components package output.
Fully typed components with a stable prop API.
BEM-style classes and scoped utilities for use on any page without a framework.
Token-driven mobile components that share the A1 design language.
Standards-based custom elements for framework-agnostic surfaces.
Explore components, read the token docs, or open the system in Storybook.

page.name: A1 0.30.0 closes the Figma loop
page.description: Editor-compatible blog detail page from A1 Web.

content.fallback: This release connects design assets, structured page definitions, configurators, and the editor so supported component work can travel in both directions.

Supported Figma instances export as A1 page-definition nodes. Their editable properties and content can be reviewed in A1 Web, and valid JSON can render back onto the Figma canvas or update the selected instance.
Runtime behavior such as event handlers, portal positioning, live data, keyboard interaction, and application logic remains owned by React and the host app.
Visual decisions remain editable in design, structured decisions remain reviewable as JSON, and behavior stays with the runtime that can test it.
A practical bridge for building with A1 assets, checking design-system compatibility, and exchanging structured pages, patterns, and component data between Figma and the local A1 workspace.
Add governed A1 assets, convert compatible selections, and apply focused repairs.
Inspect a selection for A1 compatibility and create a visible design-system report.
Preview structured JSON and explicitly sync linked project pages.
The plugin preserves the parts Figma can represent and names the parts that must stay with production code.
Playground handoffs and linked-page sync use the localhost bridge. Queues are held in memory and the plugin is opened manually.

content.fallback: Buttons trigger actions, submit forms, and navigate people through a task. Choose one clear primary action per decision area.
Begin with a verb that describes the outcome, such as “Save changes” or “Add to project.” Avoid generic labels when the destination or result can be named.
